Online:Mender's Bond:
{{Trail|Scribing}}
[[File:ON-icon-book-grimoire-Restoration Staff.png|right]]
:''Tether yourself to an ally, manifesting a life link between you and them.''

'''Mender's Bond''' is a [[ON:Scribing|Scribed]] skill [[ON:Scribing#Grimoires|Grimoire]] on the [[ON:Restoration Staff|Restoration Staff]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Restoration Staff Master|Restoration Staff Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character. 
It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  Prior to [[ON:Update 44|Update 44]], this grimoire was unique in that it was the only one whose name does not change based on your choice of Focus Script.  It was always just "Mender's Bond".

Mender's Bond creates a tether between you and a target.  The target of Mender's Bond can be any ally, whether another player, a [[ON:Companions|companion]], or many friendly NPCs.  (The only exception to this seems to be that the Mitigation Focus script can target other players or companions, but ''not'' other NPCs.)  Depending on your choice of scripts, either allies or enemies (possibly both) standing between you and the target, "in the link" as the descriptions say, will be affected in some way.

*Cast Time: Instant
*Range: 20 meters
*Duration: 12 seconds
*Cost: {{ESO Magicka Link|3969}}

'''Vault''' is a Scribed skill Grimoire, on the [[ON:Bow|Bow]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Bow Master|Bow Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character. 
It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  The name of the scribed skill changes depending upon your choice of Focus Script.

In order to use this skill effectively, you need to pay attention to what's behind you in order to avoid falling off a cliff or into another hazard, or alerting more enemies.  The safest thing to do may be to maneuver yourself so that your back is to a wall.  You can also take advantage of the fact that you generally cannot jump to a higher elevation than where you started.  So casting the skill while facing downwards on a slope or stairway will prevent you from going too far back when flipping.  Also be aware that the skill has a tendency to double-cast (most likely because you cast it while still in the middle of another attack animation, so you don't jump immediately and press the key twice not realizing that the first cast was just delayed).  So in locations where falling off the edge is a real danger (e.g. boss fights in the [[ON:Infinite Archive|Infinite Archive]]), you might want to avoid using this skill at all.

*Target: Area
*Radius: 6 meters

{{Trail|Scribing}}
[[File:ON-icon-book-grimoire-Dual Wield.png|right]]
:''Twirl and throw an enchanted dagger at an enemy, which returns to you after a short delay and hits additional enemies in the path.''

'''Traveling Knife''' is a Scribed skill Grimoire, on the [[ON:Dual Wield|Dual Wield]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Dual Wield Master|Dual Wield Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character.

It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  The name of the scribed skill changes depending upon your choice of Focus Script.

Traveling Knife causes you to throw a knife at an enemy target, which causes damage to the target, and then to any enemies between the target and you on return (except for Shattering Knife, which damages other enemies around the target instead).  The exact effects depend on your choice of scripts.

The trick to using this skill is that in order to get the most effect from it, you want to target the most distant opponent in a group, so that it hits as many other targets as possible on the way back.  This can be difficult as the game generally wants to prioritize closer targets.  You can of course move between the throw and the return to line up more potential targets.  One thing to note is that you always throw with your right hand and catch with your left.  This means that it's easier to throw to the right side of the closer targets and then move to the left than it is to do the reverse.  (Shattering Knife makes this irrelevant, of course.)

*Cast Time: Instant
*Target: Enemy
*Range: 15 meters
